extracted.intended_audience: civil society organisations, affected communities, and NGOs seeking to engage companies or bring complaints under the OECD Guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for communities and civil society on how to use the OECD Guidelines to demand and conduct meaningful stakeholder engagement with companies, and how to frame complaints to National Contact Points. Covers what counts as meaningful engagement and practical tips for outreach and complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful stakeholder engagement as part of due diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Including as part of carrying out due diligence, companies should meaningfully engage with stakeholders or their legitimate representatives, with respect to activities that may significantly impact them related to matters covered by the Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidelines and OECD due diligence guidance outline what meaningful stakeholder engagement entails. You can use the OECD Guidelines to demand that companies follow these practices when their activities may significantly impact stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure interactive engagement with relevant stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure interactive engagement with relevant stakeholders, which are defined as persons, groups, or their representatives who have rights or interests related to the Guidelines that are or may be affected by a company’s operations, products, or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the definition to argue which individuals/groups must be included in engagement (not only company-selected or convenient participants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing, two-way engagement conducted in good faith and responsive to views
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct ongoing engagement with stakeholders that is two-way, conducted in good faith by participants on both sides, and responsive to stakeholders’ views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises that engagement is not a one-off consultation or a PR exercise: companies should listen, respond, and adapt based on stakeholder input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing, accessibility, appropriateness and safety of engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure stakeholder engagement is timely, accessible, appropriate, and safe for stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement must be scheduled and designed so stakeholders can participate meaningfully (e.g., language, location, format, security); late-stage consultations that do not allow meaningful influence are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and remove barriers for people in positions of vulnerability or marginality
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and remove potential barriers to engaging for people in positions of vulnerability or marginality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take proactive steps to enable participation by those with reduced access or power (e.g., women, indigenous peoples, migrant workers, persons with disabilities), including addressing language, timing, childcare, mobility, fear of reprisal, or lack of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect stakeholder engagement as a right where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, respect and ensure stakeholder engagement as a right in and of itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some contexts engagement is not optional; companies should recognise and uphold engagement as a standing right, not merely an advisory step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage early — before business activities occur and during planning/decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Note the particular importance of engaging before business activities occur, such as in the planning and decision-making stages of projects involving, for example, intensive use of land or water that could significantly affect local communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early engagement allows stakeholders to influence project design and avoid harm; consultations that occur only after decisions are final are inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise the most severely impacted or potentially impacted stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: During complaints or outreach to companies, civil society or communities should explain why the business activity is or may significantly impact relevant stakeholders. You can urge the company to prioritise (as is permitted under the Guidelines) engagement with the most severely impacted or potentially impacted stakeholders – not just stakeholders that agree with the company or are easier to access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making complaints or seeking engagement, explicitly identify who is most affected and ask companies to prioritise those voices rather than convenient or sympathetic groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain the significance of impacts when filing complaints or seeking outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil society or communities should explain why the business activity is or may significantly impact relevant stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints and outreach should include clear, evidence-based explanations of potential or actual significant impacts to support requests for engagement or remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can be the subject of OECD Guidelines complaints (NCP complaint eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints can only be filed against two types of companies operating across borders: multinational enterprises headquartered in a country that follows the OECD Guidelines, or multinational enterprises operating in a country that follows the OECD Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this eligibility rule to determine whether filing a complaint with a National Contact Point is appropriate; governments that follow the Guidelines must establish NCPs to handle complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical uses of the OECD Guidelines for civil society
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil society can use the Guidelines to: Raise community awareness about company standards; Talk to companies to demand better conduct; File complaints when companies fall below the standards; Advocate for strong laws and policies on corporate responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are practical avenues for leveraging the Guidelines: awareness-raising, direct engagement/demand-making, formal complaints to NCPs, and policy advocacy.
